key: e:mine health and safety regulations 8.10.2.1 b
synopsis: South African sub-regulation 8.10.2.1(b) covers machine-against-machine collisions where there is significant collision risk; it commenced on 21 December 2022 through Government Gazette No. 47790, Notice 2908 [f2273]. The skeptic's review reports that this provision and companion sub-regulation 8.10.1.2(b) had been suspended in 2015 because the technology was unavailable [f10724]. Together, these provisions require automatic detection and effective warning, followed by means to retard a diesel-powered trackless mobile machine to a safe speed and automatically apply its brakes if no action is taken to prevent a potential collision [f2274, f2275]. The collision-prevention system must also fail to safe without human intervention [f2276, f10723]. The precedents chapter treats these regulations, alongside MOSH performance requirements and its verification regime, as existing off-road provisions, although the supplied facts do not specify numerical acceptance thresholds [f1713].

relations.note: Both give 21 December 2022 as the commencement date.
Adds the 2015 suspension and technology-unavailability explanation to the commencement history.
Commencement establishes the regulations as existing off-road provisions.
Specifies diesel machines, safe-speed retardation, and the no-action trigger for automatic braking.
Both state the requirement to fail to safe without human intervention.
Adds automatic detection and effective warning to the summarized braking and fail-safe requirements.
Adds retardation and automatic braking when no preventive action is taken.
